A worn or fouled DO sensor, or still water around it, can also produce falsely low readings. Temperature actually rose during the drop (to ~71.7°F), which doesn't fit the natural upwelling explanation (that would point toward cooler water).

**Suggested next steps:**
- Inspect the sensors for fouling or damage and check the pod is sitting properly in the water — especially the turbidity sensor, which should be replaced (Clean Earth Rovers support: sales@cleanearthrovers.com). Cleaning resets fouling, so compare readings before and after.

- Note what you can see from a safe distance (water color, debris, dead fish, nearby work) with times and photos, and check for activity near or upstream of the pod at the time of the change (construction, pumping, outfall discharges, boat traffic).

If you suspect a spill, your local health or environmental agency can test for fecal indicator bacteria (Enterococcus in coastal water) — the sensors can't stand in for that.
